75ncli:342: When AI agents access infrastructure through MCP servers, their prompts, queries, tool calls, and data accessed are "invisible" in traditional audit systems — without structured records, detection and tracing are impossible. Teleport treats agents as first-class identities: the SSH servers, K8s clusters, databases, and MCP servers they access all traverse the existing proxy channel, naturally inheriting session recording, RBAC, and lockdown controls; policy-compliant sessions are also forwarded to external inference services (OpenAI / Amazon Bedrock) for automatic summary generation. "Identity security" extending from humans to machine and AI identities is an extension of the same mechanism, not a new system — for enterprises adopting coding agents like Claude Code or Codex, this is a new audit and compliance surface that cannot be avoided.

d0sqes:407: Teleport does not pursue "generic anomaly detection"; instead it maintains a cross-platform detection catalog: on the AWS side it covers root activity, audit log deletion, EBS encryption changes, IAM user creation, etc.; on the GitHub side it covers 26 subcategories of security function changes including SAML/MFA/OAuth policy changes, branch protection overrides, and secret scanning alerts; on the Okta side it monitors admin MFA disablement, OAuth token reuse, dormant accounts, and excessive MFA failures. Cross-platform impossible travel detection correlates GitHub, Okta, and Teleport simultaneously, with the attack surface spanning SaaS and infrastructure. The response side is equally engineered: 1-Click Identity Lock has agents terminate matching sessions in real time at every resource layer and reject new connections, with targeting scopes and time limits to support safe rollback; Crown Jewels outputs additions and removals of access paths to critical resources as diff-form audit events, keeping alerts focused on the most important assets.
